Frances McDormand brings her trademark blend of intelligence, wit and emotional honesty to David Lindsay-Abaire's compassionate drama about class, loyalty and the choices that define us.
Smartly directed by Daniel Sullivan, the often-caustic production provides a humane, realistic and absorbing examination of ordinary people's behavior when their world is threatened.
Ms. Lindsay-Abaire has written a solidly crafted play that asks hard questions about class, loyalty and the meaning of success in contemporary America.
In the current economy of scaled-back American dreams, when the role of class is too often dismissed, Good People has a quality rarely seen on Broadway: It seems necessary.

Rabbit Hole, which he adapted for a 2010 film, focused on an attractive, accomplished couple whose seemingly charmed life was shattered by the accidental death of their 4-year-old son. In contrast, the central figure in Lindsay-Abaire's excellent new play, Good People (* * * ½ out of four), is a woman for whom things can only get better.

cn.t: Lindsay-Abaire's darkly comic drama about working-class Boston earns strong praise for its authentic portrayal of economic struggle and McDormand's powerful lead performance, though some find the play itself underwhelming.

sg.ra: SeatPlan notes rows A-D are ideal at this 634-seat house: close enough to catch facial expressions but not neck-craning. Row AA also called out for superior legroom. No overhang concerns (Mezzanine overhang starts at row G per SeatPlan).

Headout and SeatPlan both flag rows E-J as the best price-to-sightline ratio: meaningfully cheaper than the A-D premium band while staying close in a 634-seat room. Slight orchestra rake keeps sightlines clean. Mezzanine overhang (per SeatPlan) begins at row G but the intimate room means no sound-deadening issue in this band.

sg.vl: Under the overhang but still engaged
sg.ra: SeatPlan confirms the Mezzanine overhangs from row G back, so K-Q sit fully under. The room is small enough (Headout: 'one of Broadway's more intimate spaces') that rear orchestra remains engaged. Rows P and Q are accessibility-friendly (no aisle stairs per folliesbroadway). Legroom tightens beyond row O per SeatPlan.

Headout and SeatPlan both name AA-BB center as premier seats with 'clean, direct look at the stage' and elevation that improves the view. aviewfrommyseat user on Mezzanine L row A aisle reported 'lots of legroom' with only a thin safety bar as minor issue. Excellent rake across the mezzanine.

SeatPlan and Headout both emphasize that the mezzanine has 'excellent rake' keeping all rows elevated with clean sightlines; Headout says 'no truly bad seat in the house'.
